standard_prerequisites.name: A functor with an exact left adjoint preserves injectives
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the right adjoint carries injective objects to injective objects, which makes uI an injective object of the target category.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transformation of injective maps and enough injectives
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the notions of a functor transforming injective maps into injective maps and of a category with enough injectives
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the hypothesis that the embedding in the source category is preserved and the definition of enough injectives that is being verified for the target.

core_obligations: The construction (proof lines 7560-7566): for an object B of the target category one picks an injection of vB into an injective object I of the source category, which exists by the hypothesis that the source has enough injectives.

The injection into an injective object (proof lines 7564-7566): by the cited lemma and the assumptions the corresponding map from B to uI is an injection of B into an injective object, and since B was arbitrary the target category has enough injectives.
proof_roadmap: Choose an injection of the image of an arbitrary object into an injective object of the source.
Use the preservation of injectives to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if an additive functor has a right adjoint which preserves injective maps, the source category has enough injectives and the right adjoint kills no nonzero object, then the target category has enough injectives (statement lines 7545-7558). The proof is a complete argument: for an arbitrary object of the target one chooses an injection of its image into an injective object of the source, which exists by hypothesis, and the cited lemma together with the assumptions identifies the adjoint transpose as an injection of that object into an injective object (proof lines 7560-7566). The non-formal content is the use of the adjunction to transport the embedding. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
